solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Timely precaution

blocks.note: surface reading: any sensible step taken before trouble arrives
setter's reading: the first half of the proverb about a small repair made early saving nine later ones

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs '... saves nine': mending a small tear at once spares much larger mending later, which is exactly a precaution taken in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is the classic proverbial example of acting early to prevent greater work later.

clue.text: Reggae dance: special skill's being given upward jerk, not constant

indicators.note: in a down clue a jerk upwards flips the word so it reads from bottom to top
'not' tells us to drop the letter that stands for a constant in physics

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for special
a knack is a skill

explanation.surface: A dancer's special talent gets a sudden upward kick in a reggae routine.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the usual symbol for a constant (as in the speed of light), so it goes from the reversed skill.
explanation.definitionFit: The skank is a dance performed to ska and reggae music, with bent knees and swinging arms.

clue.text: As regards clue coming up — this one's a belter!

indicators.note: in a down entry, something coming up reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: re means 'with regard to'
clue (or clew) in Chambers is a ball of thread, a tangle, here a knot

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that the upcoming clue is a real cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'clue' sounds like a crossword clue, but it is the old word for a ball of thread. To tonk is to hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonker is one who tonks, i.e. strikes hard, so it is a belter in the sense of a hard hitter.

clue.text: Might such frontal markings represent Sakti?

indicators.note: to represent letters is to set them out in another form, so the name is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written: Sakti is the Hindu goddess of divine energy

explanation.surface: Could the forehead marks worn by Hindus be symbols of the goddess Sakti?
explanation.definitionFit: A tika is the coloured mark Hindus wear on the forehead, so these are markings on the front of the head.

clue.text: Memorable colt ridden by Kate

indicators.note: a horse ridden by someone has its rider sitting round it, so one name holds the other

blocks.note: Kate and Cathy are both short forms of Catherine
C is the abbreviation for colt in racing form

explanation.surface: A young horse that Kate rides sticks in the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate becomes another pet form of Catherine, and the colt's abbreviation sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune is one that is easily remembered, so catchy means memorable.

clue.text: Opponent of dualism in chair uneasily creating consonance?

indicators.note: something sitting uneasily is not settled in place, so the letters are jumbled
one element is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a monist holds that reality is one substance, against dualism's two

explanation.surface: A philosopher sits awkwardly in a chair, somehow producing agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonistic relates to harmony, so it describes something producing consonance or agreement.

clue.text: Riparian? Steersman goes into one, both losing heads

indicators.note: one word going into another ends up housed inside it
each of the two words drops its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a pilot steers a ship

explanation.surface: A river-dweller watches a helmsman fall in, both of them ending up headless.
explanation.walkthrough: Behead one to NE and the steersman to ILOT, then put the second inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nilote is a native of the Upper Nile region, so with the question mark, a riverbank dweller by example.

clue.text: Hardened clay, fired, seen in e.g. azulejo

indicators.note: something seen in another thing is held within it

blocks.note: an azulejo is a glazed Spanish or Portuguese tile
fired as in set alight

explanation.surface: Fired, hardened clay appears in a decorative Portuguese tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardened clay, fired' reads as one description of pottery, but 'fired' is a separate piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillite is a sedimentary rock formed from glacial till (boulder clay) that has been consolidated.

clue.text: Batting twice bags duck — it does stick out somewhat at the top!

definitions.text: it does stick out somewhat at the top!

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a sack, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: batting is in, written two times
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the zero shape

explanation.surface: A batsman goes in twice and collects a nought, sticking out at the top of the order.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck goes inside the second IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The inion is the bony bump at the back of the skull, which protrudes slightly at the top of the neck.

clue.text: Scotch has to fill a chap with a hint of uplift

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the opening letter is taken
to fill something is to occupy its inside

blocks.note: a chap is a man
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Scotsman must top up a fellow with a little encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' here means Scots dialect, not whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Maun is the Scots form of must, meaning 'has to'.

clue.text: Strong home-brew, not bad in a saki mixed before noon

indicators.note: a mixed drink has its ingredients stirred together, so these letters are scrambled
one element is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
not bad means OK, acceptable
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A morning cocktail of saki makes a decent, strong home-made drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Skokiaan is a potent illicit liquor brewed at home in southern Africa.

clue.text: Asthmatic's stand-by: nutty pralines, hard inside

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order
one element is placed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An asthma sufferer keeps hard nut sweets handy just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty pralines' reads as a description of sweets, but 'nutty' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spinhaler is a branded inhaler device, the kind of thing an asthma patient keeps ready.

clue.text: Self-confidence shown by e.g. American leaping over bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, leaping over turns the word head over heels so it reads upwards

blocks.note: e.g. can mean 'as', as in 'such as'
US is short for American
rance is a Scots word for a prop or bar

explanation.surface: An American athlete clearing a high-jump bar shows great self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like the athletic bar, but it is the obscure dialect word rance.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurance means a confident, self-possessed manner, a synonym for self-confidence.

clue.text: Jock's hanging border given the thumbs-down, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the word is matched by its pronunciation

blocks.note: given the thumbs-down means criticised harshly

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's curtain fringe gets a poor review.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is crossword slang for a Scot, so the definition flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pand in Scots is a valance, the short drapery hung round a bed frame.

clue.text: Wind in sequence overturned perennial

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so the word is read backwards
one element is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a suit is a sequence or set, as in cards
to wind thread is to roll it up

explanation.surface: A recurring wind in a series of events knocks over a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollius, the globeflower, is a genus of hardy perennial plants.

clue.text: Sepia container, trendy — then drum rolls?

indicators.note: a thing that rolls over turns end over end, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a drum is a barrel or cask

explanation.surface: A fashionable brown-ink pot, followed by a drumroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Sepia is the dark ink of the cuttlefish as well as the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The ink sac is the organ of a cuttlefish that holds sepia ink.

clue.text: Scottish isle ay denied short stops

indicators.note: what is denied is refused, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: Colonsay is an island in the Inner Hebrides
taken as written; ay is Scots for yes

explanation.surface: On a Scottish island, saying yes is refused for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark indicating a pause shorter than a full stop.

clue.text: Mouldy game I found in store

indicators.note: items found in a store are held inside it

blocks.note: a fund is a store or stock
go is the Japanese board game
taken as written

explanation.surface: I discovered a rotten old game in the storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungoid means like a fungus, and mould is a fungus, so mouldy is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Whist excursion, for crying out loud

blocks.note: whist is an old interjection meaning hush
an outing is a trip

explanation.surface: A card-game outing that ends in exasperation: for crying out loud!
explanation.walkthrough: Whist looks like the card game, but it is an archaic call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting is calling out at high volume, the same act as crying out loud.

clue.text: Divine sun outside in Cannes, but with half of us inside

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is a single letter, the opening one here
one element is placed within the other

blocks.note: hors is French for outside
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Sunbathing outside in Cannes, but with half our party indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Cannes' signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed Egyptian god of the sky, identified with the sun.

clue.text: Addict run aground and abandoned, one taken in

indicators.note: the word 'and' within abandoned is to be abandoned, dropped from the word
something taken in is held inside

blocks.note: to strand a ship is to run it aground
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug user runs a boat aground and is deserted, with one person taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a piece of the wordplay, not a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoner is slang for a habitual cannabis user, someone who gets stoned.

clue.text: Liqueur: take sample from costliest regardless

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion lifted from inside a larger whole

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Taste the liqueur from the priciest bottles, whatever they cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Strega is an Italian herbal liqueur coloured yellow by saffron.

clue.text: Take that (last one going to head)! It could render you senseless

indicators.note: the final letter moves to the front of the word, rotating it

blocks.note: 'there!' is an exclamation like 'take that!'

explanation.surface: A fighter cries 'Take that!' while landing a knockout blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was once widely used as a general anaesthetic, which makes a patient unconscious.

clue.text: Left in place sacred to Muslims, wherein blacks predominate

indicators.note: one element is placed inside the other

blocks.note: harem originally meant a sacred or forbidden place
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Something left in a holy Muslim place where dark colours dominate.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem is the New York district historically known as a centre of Black American life and culture.

clue.text: Very sorry journey ends prematurely in story

indicators.note: finishing early means the final letter is dropped
one element is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a conte is a short story
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A tale whose journey ends too soon leaves everyone very sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite means feeling deep remorse for wrongdoing, so very sorry.

clue.text: Male for head left off helmet? He's belted!

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is left off it

blocks.note: a morion is a crested 16th-century helmet
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man takes off his helmet and gets punched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belted' suggests being hit, but it means wearing a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion the hunter constellation has three stars in a row known as Orion's Belt.

clue.text: Stand? Eton turns to pop superstar with this

blocks.clueFragment: Eton turns to pop superstar with this
blocks.note: add an L after the E of Eton and it becomes Elton, as in Elton John

explanation.surface: Pupils from Eton become pop stars with a stand to prop them up.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'E's L' (an L for the E) turns Eton into Elton; that phrase is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds a painting or board upright.

clue.text: Mandarin (of a kind) one in this country has reared

indicators.note: one element is placed inside the other
in a down clue, rearing up makes the word read from bottom to top

blocks.note: for a British newspaper, this country is the UK
one in the sense of anyone, as 'you' is used generally

explanation.surface: A Chinese official of a sort has been raised in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuo-yu is the national standard spoken form of Chinese, based on Mandarin.

clue.text: Lecturer on ancient Greek capital — such should not be hurried

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lecturer
Argos was a powerful ancient Greek city-state

explanation.surface: A lecturer speaks on an old Greek city in a leisurely way.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a slow, broad movement in music, so it must be played without haste.

clue.text: Make down payment on what goes into strong ale (not by round)

indicators.note: the letters spelling 'by' that sit round the outside are removed

blocks.note: barley wine is a strong ale, and barley is its main grain

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit on the malt for a strong beer, but not for a whole round.
explanation.walkthrough: The grain begins with B and ends with Y, the letters of 'by' wrapped round the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: To arle is an old Scots verb meaning to give earnest money, a deposit to seal a bargain.

clue.text: Take a turn off for commuters' short cut?

indicators.note: something off has gone bad or wrong, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: R stands for 'recipe', Latin for take, on prescriptions
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver turns off the main road to find a quicker route to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat run is a minor road that drivers use to avoid traffic at rush hour.

clue.text: White crystalline mineral: see iron mixed with it (early English cladding)

indicators.note: mixed things are stirred together, so these letters are rearranged
cladding is an outer covering, so these letters wrap round the rest

blocks.note: EE is the abbreviation for Early English
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A white mineral blended with iron, used as an old English facing material.
explanation.walkthrough: Early English is an architectural style and the old form of the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Erionite is a zeolite mineral occurring as white woolly crystals.

clue.text: Group with common purpose housed in pueblo compound

indicators.note: something housed in a place is lodged inside it, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A like-minded group lives together in a Native American village enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: A pueblo is an adobe village of the American Southwest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of countries or parties acting together for shared aims.

clue.text: Jeweller's mineral, quartz-like, I tackle as of old in washing trough

indicators.note: one element is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a tye is a trough for washing ore in mining
taken as written
gere is an archaic spelling of gear, meaning tackle

explanation.surface: A jeweller finds a quartz-like gem in a miner's washing trough.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger-eye is a golden-brown chatoyant quartz used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Bamboos requiring little depth with calm sea round rippling

indicators.note: rippling water is disturbed and shifting, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for depth
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bamboo plants growing in shallow water need a calm sea that ripples gently around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dendrocalamus is a genus of giant tropical bamboos, so the name stands for these plants collectively.
